items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: Seen him and I heard him.

ctx.x: All I can know is the West Coast. And he know the band already going to have a booking to go out there. But some fellas, you see, they get head swollen like that and they say they're not used to experience traveling. And when this, Earl Hans, that was a man who had what you call original. He was, we know he come from big bands out of Chicago. You would call them swing bands, you understand? That, I know that. Seen him and I heard him. And they form a band, a Dixieland group in San Francisco. And when they sent…
How come that Joe got back into the band and you left?

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: Earl Hines, man, you sure did, yeah. They was working at the Hangover Club in San Francisco.

ctx.x: Did you ever enjoy joining Earl Hines?

Earl Hines, man, you sure did, yeah. They was working at the Hangover Club in San Francisco. Yeah. And we did two weeks up there and then we come down to L.A. and they had three months, but I didn't stay. I came on back and Joe was released off his job and I placed him back with the band. Yeah. I came back down, yeah, and I've been playing ever since. That's where I joined the outfit with Kid Howard and them at City Village Place. Yeah. And from there we went over to Poesie Hunt and Emma. I've been playing with…

That covers, I think most of your jobs pretty well. We might talk for a few minutes we have left. Yeah. But you can remember anything else about your father and the type of music he played or any early bands he might have played in?
